review-verify and review-finalpass fall through to review\\u0027s value before anything below it, matching how their models resolve; the existing node-wide --effort keeps its meaning as the level beneath every role value\u0022,\u0022A project and a task each carry one optional effort: h9k project set \\u003Cproject\\u003E --effort \\u003Clevel|default\\u003E and h9k task revise \\u003Cid\\u003E --effort \\u003Clevel|default\\u003E; a session\\u0027s effort resolves in this order, the first level set wins: the task\\u0027s value, then the project\\u0027s value, then the node\\u0027s value for the session\\u0027s role, then the node-wide value, then unset so the model\\u0027s own default decides; h9k project show and h9k task show print the value when set\u0022,\u0022Every session the daemon launches, and every session h9k task start or h9k task delegate launches, gets the effort resolved for its own role, task, and project written into its settings file as effortLevel; the spawn request carries the role so the executor resolves it in one place rather than at each dispatch site; a session with nothing set at any level leaves the key out of the file exactly as today; the interactive role is excluded, a session a person sits in honors their own user-level setting\u0022,\u0022The four level names and the resolution chain live in the domain as vendor-neutral values (AgentEffort and the resolve function), with the Claude Code effortLevel key known only to the Claude executor and its settings-file writer; no vendor string appears in the domain or in the CLI\\u0027s stored settings, so a second executor adds one mapping and touches no resolution code\u0022,\u0022h9k config show prints one effort line per role beneath the node-wide line, each naming its value and origin (config file, environment, or which level it falls through to), and h9k daemon status prints the same rows for the settings a daemon started now would bind, in the same shape the per-role model lines already use\u0022,\u0022A test over the resolve function proves the chain with a task value winning over a project value, a project value winning over a node role value, a role value winning over the node-wide value, one role falling through to unset, and review-verify falling to review; the project\\u0027s single model now overrides the node\\u0027s per-role table instead of sitting beneath it\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Refactor\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian, 2026-09-26 12:46 EDT, in the hall9k project window, ruled at the walk of 6fe2f5a2 (per-role effort) that the override order for effort is task over project over node, the further down the higher the priority, and that the model chain should read the same. Today DaemonOptions.ResolveModel (src/Hall9k.Daemon/DaemonOptions.cs near line 799) calls AgentModel.Resolve(taskModel, ModelByRole.For(role), projectModel, DefaultModel), so the node\\u0027s per-role value beats the project\\u0027s single value (Decisions Log #33). This task flips the middle two so the project\\u0027s value beats the node\\u0027s role value; the verify and final-pass chains (ResolveVerifyReviewModel near line 821, ResolveFinalFullPassModel near line 848) and ResolveCourierModel near line 877 follow the same reorder. Update the doc comments, PLAN.md\\u0027s #33 projection if it states the order, docs/cli.md and docs/concepts.md where they describe the chain, and the existing resolution tests. No project on Brian\\u0027s fleet sets a project model today (verified with h9k project show on all four Mac projects, 2026-09-26), so nothing live changes behavior. Not stacked on 6fe2f5a2: the two touch different functions and can merge in either order; both should be released before effort is documented as mirroring the model chain. Dispatched sessions must not run install, update, join, or reconcile against the live install.
